newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Optus says Seven settlement unlikely.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Optus says Seven settlement unlikely.

text.p: Optus Communications Pty Ltd said on Wednesday it does not expect to reach a settlement with Seven Network Ltd prior to Monday's court hearing on ligitation between Seven and Optus Communications associate Optus Vision.
But Optus chief executive Ziggy Switkowski said he did not rule out any settlement with Seven by Monday.
"We have got lines of communication in place but I think the overwhelming probability at this stage is that we will meet in court on Monday," Switkowski told reporters.
He said Optus planned to get its float underway probably in the second half of calendar 1997.
Switkowski said Optus was mindful of the Telstra privatisation schedule which would have to be factored into Optus' float plans at some stage.
The government plans to sell a third of Telstra.
"Yes there is a chance we might buff up against it, but that is not our plan," Switkowski said.
Asked if the possibility of Optus' proposed float would coincide with Telstra's float was a worry, he said: "It has not been until now."
He added the company's concerns had been focussed on litigation with the Seven Network.
Seven Network is 24 percent owned by its chairman kerry Stokes and 15 percent owned by News Corp Ltd.

Switkowski earlier told a business luncheon Optus' first half performance had been in line with expecations. Optus is half year result due out next Tuesday. Asked if those expectations were fairly lofty, he said: "Well yes."
Switkowski said Optus' full revenue for the 1996/97 year was expected to be "north of A$2 billion."
He said he was very pleased with the subscriber growth of the Optus Vision pay television service.
"The last revelation was 100,000 in September 1996 and we have moved strongly beyond that," he said.
